newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* The Federal Reserve has decided to leave interest rates unchanged.
* Dell Computer Corp posted earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations.
* Galileo International Partnership, an electronic reservations company, has agreed to buy Apollo Travel Services for $700 million.
* Toy Biz Inc has pulled out of a proposal to combine some units with Marvel Entertainment Group Inc.
* Home Depot Inc, Dayton Hudson Corp and AnnTaylor Stores Corp all reported strong earnings.
* Honda Motor Co Ltd saw its quarterly profits more than double.
* Apple Computer Inc Executive Vice President for Operations George Scalise has resigned to become president of the Semiconductor Industry Association.
* Singapore pulled in a first ranking and the U.S. was third in a study of 53 countries ranked for economic potential.

* Insiders at Xircom Inc who sold their shares high then turned around and bought shares at a low may be forced to turn over some or all of their profits under Securites and Exchange Commission rules.
* The federal Environmental Protection Agency has recommended new rules to require paper mills to reduce their emissions of dioxins and other toxic chemicals.
* The Clinton Administration proposed creating a special board to oversee efforts to modernize the Internal Revenue Service.
* Executives from more than 100 companies have pledged to hire more people from public assistance rolls.
* A federal judge has stripped away much of the copyright protections claimed by a legal publishing unit of Thomson Corp .
* With or without intervention by the Federal Reserve, the U.S. economy appears headed into a period of slower economic growth.
* Karel van Miert, the European Commission's minister for competition, has been a needle in the side of a plan by Boeing Co to complete its $14 billion takeover of the McDonnell Douglas Corp.
